name: GEORGIA

flag.title: Flag of Georgia
flag.note: White with red cross & four red crosses

lead: Georgia sits between the Caucasus mountains and the Black Sea. People made the first wine here 8,000 years ago. Georgian singers weave three voices together, and one song flew into space. Its alphabet is found nowhere else.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Founded c. 458 AD by hot springs

geo: Georgia lies where Europe meets Asia. Snowy mountains form a giant wall in the north. Mount Shkhara rises 5,201 m, taller than any peak in the Alps.
The west is warm and wet from Black Sea breezes. Hot mineral springs bubble up in the city of Tbilisi.
animals: The East Caucasian tur is a wild goat with curved horns. The Caucasian leopard is the world's largest kind of leopard.
Each autumn, over one million birds of prey fly past Batumi, a Black Sea port. The Caucasian salamander lives in the western rainforests.
culture: Georgians have made wine for 8,000 years in qvevri, clay jars buried underground. Grape juice slowly turns into wine in the cool earth. UNESCO listed this method in 2013.
Georgian polyphonic singing (three voices, each with its own tune) is among the oldest music on Earth. The oldest form of the Georgian alphabet dates to the 5th century.
history: Western Georgia was once Colchis, where the Greek hero Jason sought the Golden Fleece (a magic sheepskin). By the 11th century, a Georgian kingdom reached the Caspian Sea.
Russia took over in the 19th century, then the Russian-led Soviet Union in 1921. Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991, and it still guards its old identity.
wows: Traces of the world's oldest wine, 8,000 years old, were found near Tbilisi, Georgia's capital.
The Georgian song Chakrulo flew into space in 1977 on Voyager, a space probe.
Dmanisi in Georgia has early-human skulls 1.8 million years old, among the oldest found outside Africa.
Legend says a king’s falcon dropped its prey into hot springs, and Tbilisi grew there.
Over one million birds of prey fly past the port of Batumi each autumn.
Georgia has over 500 local grape types, more than almost any other country.
Georgia's alphabet has three ancient forms, all UNESCO heritage.

myths.myth: Georgia is named after Saint George
myths.fact: Many experts think the name comes from Gurj, a Persian word. Georgians call their land Sakartvelo.

myths.myth: Georgian cheese bread is just pizza
myths.fact: It is khachapuri. The boat-shaped kind holds a runny egg and butter.
